spine: 1. 作者把 Valen 的借用檢查放進三個記憶體安全挑戰之中，這篇只處理第一個：更寬鬆的借用檢查器。
2. 基礎是單一所有權：每份資料一個擁有者，所以每個物件只有一條路徑，路徑由起點加成員、[]、變體組成。
3. 參照記住路徑；修改一條路徑讓指向它裡面的參照失效，指向它本身的不失效；錯誤在使用失效參照時才報。
4. 函式簽名（in 與 mut）宣告會動到哪些路徑，只有一種參照，可變性由周圍函式決定。
5. 與傳統的差別：shared-xor-mutable 放寬成 no use-after-free；作者用 step 範例做定性比較，並自己加了保留。
6. 三個延伸：mutable-in-immutable、temporary uniqueness（Rust 互通）、wildcard descendant path。
7. 未定案的部分：type-stability 例外尚未實作，unique group、最佳化器好處、參照計數當陣列都是推測或預告。

perspective.mechanism: 路徑加失效規則：每個物件一條路徑，參照記住路徑，修改或呼叫帶 mut 的函式時，指向被動到路徑裡面的參照失效，使用失效參照才報編譯錯誤。
perspective.tradeoff: 把 shared-xor-mutable 放寬成 no use-after-free，換來多個可寫參照與局部可變權限，代價是函式簽名要宣告修改的路徑；作者自承零執行期成本有爭議、速度優勢不必然。
perspective.reader_use: 台灣的系統程式工程師可用文中的路徑與失效規則，檢視自己在 Rust 裡為了借用規則所做的結構妥協，並等後續實作篇再判斷這套設計是否站得住。

notes.quote: I've long suspected that to find the holy grail, we'd have to solve three memory-safety challenges:
notes.interpretation: 作者用 suspected 表達這是他長期的推測，不是已證明的事。

notes.quote: Can we make a more relaxed borrow checker?
notes.interpretation: 第一個挑戰：更寬鬆的借用檢查器。

notes.quote: Can we make a borrow checker read more complex data?
notes.interpretation: 第二個挑戰。

notes.quote: Can we make those two systems work together at the same time?
notes.interpretation: 第三個挑戰。

notes.quote: This post mainly focuses on the first piece: Valen's more relaxed borrow checker.
notes.interpretation: 本篇只談第一個挑戰。

notes.quote: Valen's approach is built on the "Group Borrowing" proposal which was designed by my friend Nick Smith.
notes.interpretation: 提案出自 Nick Smith，作者稱他為朋友。

notes.quote: But group borrowing actually resolves the conflict, by relaxing "shared-xor-mutable" to "no use-after-free".
notes.interpretation: 核心替換：shared-xor-mutable 放寬成 no use-after-free。post 只以術語轉述，未整句引用。

notes.quote: Group borrowing gives a program memory safety without run-time cost.
notes.interpretation: 作者宣稱沒有執行期成本，但腳註立刻加上 n09 的保留。

notes.quote: Though it's debatable if any language can get memory safety with zero run-time cost.
notes.interpretation: 作者自承零執行期成本的說法有爭議。

notes.quote: It catches use-after-free problems at compile time, and it does it in a way that has less restrictions than previous approaches.
notes.interpretation: 編譯期抓 use-after-free，限制比先前做法少。

notes.quote: Every object is described by a path, according to single ownership.
notes.interpretation: 五件機制之一。

notes.quote: Every reference remembers the path of the object it's pointing to.
notes.interpretation: 五件機制之二。

notes.quote: When we destroy an object, everything pointing at its path is no longer usable.
notes.interpretation: 五件機制之三：銷毀時，指向該路徑的一切失效。

notes.quote: A function signature describes the paths it modifies.
notes.interpretation: 五件機制之四：簽名描述會修改的路徑。

notes.quote: When we call a function, everything pointing inside its modified paths are no longer usable.
notes.interpretation: 五件機制之五：呼叫函式時，指向被修改路徑裡面的一切失效。

notes.quote: Valen's borrow checker is based on single ownership, like C++ and Rust.
notes.interpretation: 基礎是單一所有權。

notes.quote: Every value is "owned" by a containing object, array, stack frame, or global.
notes.interpretation: 擁有者可能是外層物件、陣列、堆疊框或全域變數。post 以中文轉述未直接引用。

notes.quote: Every piece of data has only one owner (because single ownership), so every object has one path.
notes.interpretation: 單一擁有者推出每個物件一條路徑。post 中「檢查器大概不必追持有者」是我的推論，文中已明標為推論；來源腳註 36 另說物件可能有多條路徑（見 n70）。

notes.quote: When we modify an object, we mark any reference pointing inside that object as "invalidated".
notes.interpretation: 修改物件時，指向其裡面的參照被標成 invalidated。

notes.quote: We don't invalidate references pointing to an object. We invalidate references pointing inside the object.
notes.interpretation: 失效的方向：指向物件本身的不失效，指向裡面的失效。

notes.quote: That invalidates all references pointing inside vec.
notes.interpretation: vec 範例：push 修改 vec，elem_ref 失效，vec_ref 仍可用（程式碼註解與文字 we can still use vec_ref 支持）。post 對 Vec 搬動的動機是標記過的推測。

notes.quote: Valen, however, has only one kind of borrow reference.
notes.interpretation: 只有一種借用參照。

notes.quote: In Valen, the mutability of something isn't part of its type, the surrounding function determines it.
notes.interpretation: 可變性由周圍函式決定，不在型別上。

notes.quote: let first_ref = &world.entities[0];
notes.interpretation: first_ref 範例第 3 行，指向第 0 個元素。範例其餘行：world.entities = Vec<Entity>.new(); 與 return first_ref.hp;，結尾註解 Compile error: Used a borrow after invalidated。

notes.quote: the compiler invalidated all references pointing inside it
notes.interpretation: 重新指派 world.entities 讓裡面的參照失效。

notes.quote: the compiler sees we're using first_ref, so shows an error.
notes.interpretation: 報錯發生在使用處。post 中「失效後不再使用就不報錯」是從此句推得的推論，已標記為推論。

notes.quote: in means "a reference to one of".
notes.interpretation: in 的意思。

notes.quote: Put together: entity is a reference to one of world's entities's elements, and we can modify it.
notes.interpretation: in 加 mut 的完整解讀，另有 mut there means "we can modify it."。

notes.quote: push has to say so, in its signature, with the mut keyword.
notes.interpretation: 修改資訊來自簽名；文章另說編譯器看到 mut(self)、知道 self 是 vec，便知道 vec 被修改。檢查器是否讀函式本體，文章沒提，post 以我讀到的範圍限定。

notes.quote: doesn't invalidate the entity
notes.interpretation: step_and_read 範例：step 只改 entity 內容（程式碼註解 Only modifies an entity's contents.），所以 entity 仍可用。

notes.quote: Vanilla Rust was memory-safe, but a little slower, and a little more complex.
notes.interpretation: 作者對一般 Rust 版 step 的定性描述。

notes.quote: Adding GhostCell gave us the same speed as C++, but it's still a bit complex.
notes.interpretation: GhostCell 版速度同 C++ 但仍稍複雜。文章在此未另述其安全性。

notes.quote: With Valen's approach, we get something fast, safe, and simple:
notes.interpretation: 作者對 Valen 版 step 的定性描述。

notes.quote: Of course, the above requires care to uphold memory safety, since C++ doesn't check for memory safety at compile time.
notes.interpretation: C++ 版要靠人維持記憶體安全。

notes.quote: Valen adds this so that we don't have to do the classic borrow-checking pattern of taking in the entire world mutably.
notes.interpretation: mutable-in-immutable 的目的。圖上對整個 world 的失效結果是我依規則的推演，已在文中說明。

notes.quote: I suspect this feature could make Valen code optimize better.
notes.interpretation: 作者推測可改善最佳化，語氣為 suspect。

notes.quote: This might require patches to LLVM to make it better able to harness the information.
notes.interpretation: 可能需要修補 LLVM；腳註另說 LLVM 以 noalias 思考而非 read-only。

notes.quote: This won't necessarily mean Valen will be faster than C++, Rust, etc.
notes.interpretation: 速度優勢不必然。

notes.quote: I think you can do extra refactoring or use unsafe in those languages to get equivalent speedups.
notes.interpretation: 作者認為其他語言靠額外重構或 unsafe 能追平，語氣為 I think。

notes.quote: However, we should be careful here too, because that same purpose can be served by other features in theory.
notes.interpretation: 出自 Wildcard Descendant Paths 一節：作者猜萬用後代路徑可用來藏起簽名的內部細節，並提醒同樣的目的理論上可由其他功能達成。與最佳化器的好處無關。

notes.quote: We can hand a Valen reference into a Rust &mut if it's the only reference that can reach that data during that call.
notes.interpretation: temporary uniqueness 規則之一。

notes.quote: If we have multiple Valen references that can point to the same object, they can only be handed into Rust & references.
notes.interpretation: temporary uniqueness 規則之二。

notes.quote: I suspect Valen can have something like a
notes.interpretation: 後接引號內的 unique group；作者推測 Valen 可有類似 unique group 的東西，是構想。

notes.quote: This is called a wildcard descendant path, and it definitely needs a better name.
notes.interpretation: 作者自認名稱不好。

notes.quote: But alas! Valen can't infer the in self.gem from the Rust code.
notes.interpretation: Valen 無法從 Rust 程式碼推出 in self.gem；標註如何寫，文章在被引用段落未說，post 中屬標記過的推測。

notes.quote: func gem(self &Chest) -> &Gem in self.gem... { &self.gem }
notes.interpretation: 萬用後代路徑的範例；文章說明 in self.gem... 表示 points somewhere inside self.gem。

notes.quote: points somewhere inside self.gem
notes.interpretation: 萬用後代路徑的意義。

notes.quote: group borrowing understands arrays
notes.interpretation: 原句為 It occurred to me: group borrowing understands arrays.；post 只引用後半。靈感來源，用於把參照計數物件描述成陣列。

notes.quote: A "multi-typed group", similar to a Vale region, as opposed to vanilla group borrowing where every group needs a type.
notes.interpretation: 要做到參照計數當陣列所需的新概念之一，尚在設想。

notes.quote: References into the run-time group don't get invalidated.
notes.interpretation: 另一個新概念 run-time group：指向它的參照不失效。尚在設想。

notes.quote: In the next few articles, I'll explain more about how we'll blend in reference counting and generational references, and how Valen's group borrow checker is implemented.
notes.interpretation: 後續文章預告。結尾另有 This is just the tip of the iceberg, so stay tuned。

notes.quote: This part isn't implemented in Valen yet. Stay tuned!
notes.interpretation: type-stability 例外尚未實作。

notes.quote: Generalizing a bit, group borrowing will never invalidate any type-stable data.
notes.interpretation: 例外的一般化描述（針對尚未實作的功能）。

notes.quote: It only invalidates pointers pointing inside any type-unstable things (enums' contents, pointer's pointee).
notes.interpretation: 只讓指在型別不穩定內容裡的指標失效。

notes.quote: Doesn't invalidate terrain_ref!
notes.interpretation: Level 範例的程式碼註解（add_entity 之後 terrain_ref 不失效）；Level 含 terrain 與 entities、location_to_entity 兩個 HashMap。

notes.quote: Group borrowing was dead before it had the chance to succeed.
notes.interpretation: 作者描述提案在 Mojo 未被採用的結果；另有 originally designed with Mojo in mind 與 despite my best efforts I couldn't convince the higher-ups that we should use it。

notes.quote: Google's Carbon language pivoted completely to group borrowing
notes.interpretation: 作者的轉述，我未查證 Carbon 的說法。

notes.quote: Plecra's exclusion typing is redesigning the Rust borrow checker with concepts from group borrowing and GhostCell.
notes.interpretation: 作者的轉述，我未查證 Plecra 的說法。

notes.quote: originally designed with Mojo in mind
notes.interpretation: 提案原本是為 Mojo 設計。

notes.quote: Having multiple local variables that point to the same object, and write through any of them (like above).
notes.interpretation: 放寬後可行寫法之一。

notes.quote: Having multiple function parameters that point to the same object, and write through any of them.
notes.interpretation: 可行寫法之二。

notes.quote: Make a "rollback" struct, that will change an object when it goes out of scope
notes.interpretation: 可行寫法之三。

notes.quote: Having multiple structs that have mutable references to a common subsystem.
notes.interpretation: 可行寫法之四。

notes.quote: Rust is generally nice to work with, but in some cases (like this one), it isn't quite as fast or simple as the C++ case
notes.interpretation: C++ 版相對較快較簡單，作為比較基準。

notes.quote: Local variable (like world).
notes.interpretation: 路徑起點之一；另兩種為 A function parameter. 與 A function's "group parameter" (we'll see this later).。

notes.quote: [] to name the elements of a collection (like above).
notes.interpretation: 路徑延伸之一；另兩種為 .diameter to name a member (like above). 與 .SomeType to name a union's variant.。原文 elements 帶強調標記，此處為去除標記後的文字。

notes.quote: somewhere in the group
notes.interpretation: 文章對 entity in world.entities[] 的口語描述，並未給 group 正式定義；原句為 entity in world.entities[] points at somewhere in the group of objects that live in the entities array。

notes.quote: This is just the tip of the iceberg
notes.interpretation: 結尾預告後續文章。

notes.quote: If you add group borrowing and a few other mechanisms, you get Valen.
notes.interpretation: 單一所有權階梯的最後一階；前三階為 C++（regular (unrestricted) pointers and references）、Vale（generational references and region borrowing）、Rust（exclusivity-checked references）。

notes.quote: This isn't strictly true; objects can actually be reached through multiple paths, if we use things like associated groups. That's a whole topic for another time though.
notes.interpretation: 腳註 36：一個物件一條路徑並非絕對，透過 associated group 之類可有多條路徑；作者說這是改天再談的題目，未說是哪一篇。

notes.quote: In Rust, we need a &mut Entity for entity_mut.advance() , and then have to throw it away to get the containing &World back to give to the get_collision_for_entity call. Then later, we need to re-fetch the &mut Entity for the resolve call.
notes.interpretation: 腳註 26：Rust 版 step 需丟掉 &mut Entity 再重新取回。bounds check 並非出自此腳註，而是範例程式碼註解（n72）。

notes.quote: bounds check, possible panic
notes.interpretation: Rust 範例程式碼中每次 &world.entities[entity_id] 取用旁的註解（共三處）。

notes.quote: nodes aren't automatically deleted when their parents are.
notes.interpretation: 腳註 27：把異質樹攤平成多個陣列的取捨之一（失去部分 RAII 好處）。

notes.quote: Also, if you split into parallel collections too much, you might risk "ID chasing" cache-miss slowdowns.
notes.interpretation: 腳註 27：拆成平行集合太多可能有 ID chasing 的 cache miss 變慢風險，語氣為 might。

notes.quote: You can generally rearrange your Rust code to match group borrowing's speed
notes.interpretation: 腳註 29 對 step 比較表的保留：一般 Rust 通常可重排程式碼追上 group borrowing 的速度（原句後接 even without GhostCell）。

notes.quote: Take a parameter pointing at an object, and another parameter pointing somewhere inside that object, and write through only the latter (we'll see this in the next section).
notes.interpretation: 五種寫法中的第二種（原列表共五項，前面 n60 至 n63 加此項）。

notes.quote: this won't invalidate callers' references to entities
notes.interpretation: 原句：This is good because this won't invalidate callers' references to entities. 只說指向 entities（而非裡面）的參照不失效；不等於所有參照都不受牽連。

notes.quote: if we describe reference-counted classes to a borrow checker as if it's a bunch of arrays, then we might be able to have borrow references into them in a memory-safe way.
notes.interpretation: 作者的設想語氣為 might be able，不是已做到；post 保留「也許」。

notes.quote: auto-deref, directly indexing a struct ( my_vec[0] ), and inferring types from groups ( entity in world.entities[] ) are coming in November.
notes.interpretation: 作者對尚未提供的語法糖的預告；屬未來承諾，可能變動，post 以「作者預告」限定。

notes.quote: in today's compiler, one needs to manually dereference, index into arrays directly like my_vec.data[0] instead of the struct, and put types on all parameters
notes.interpretation: 腳註 6：目前編譯器須手動 dereference、直接索引陣列、替所有參數寫型別。

notes.quote: plus a few other options that I'll get into later.
notes.interpretation: 路徑延伸除了 .member、[]、.SomeType 外還有其他選項，故 post 不稱「三種」為全部。

claims.note: Code lines match the source verbatim; scrubber states are consistent with it.

claims.claim_text: 圖：push 動到 world.entities 使 R2、R3 失效；step 動到 world.entities[] 只使 R3 失效；改動整個 world 使 R1-R3 失效；指向路徑本身的照常可用
claims.location: annotated figure (+ JS) and para 'step 那一列'
claims.evidence: We don't invalidate references pointing to an object. We invalidate references pointing inside the object.
claims.note: All three table rows and the JS inside() logic are consistent with the article's rule (inside = strictly longer path prefix). Post discloses it is a derivation (figcaption, 推演). Persistence of invalidation is also an unstated assumption but disclosed.

claims.claim_text: Valen 只有一種借用參照；可變性不在型別上，由周圍函式決定
claims.evidence: In Valen, the mutability of something isn't part of its type, the surrounding function determines it.

claims.claim_text: step(world &World, entity in world.entities[] mut)：in 是「a reference to one of」，mut 是「we can modify it」
claims.evidence: Put together: entity is a reference to one of world 's entities 's elements, and we can modify it.

claims.claim_text: push 必須在簽名用 mut 說明會修改；編譯器看到 mut(self)、知道 self 是 vec，便知道 vec 被修改；文章沒提檢查器要讀函式本體
claims.evidence: The compiler then sees the mut(self) , knows self is actually vec , so knows vec was mut ated.
claims.note: Absence claim is scoped to 'what I read' and the downstream inference is marked.

claims.claim_text: step_and_read 先呼叫 step 再讀 entity，註解「Only modifies an entity's contents」，step 並未讓 entity 失效
claims.evidence: this step_and_read is calling the above step function which doesn't invalidate the entity .
claims.note: R2 usable/R3 invalid is labeled the post's model.

claims.claim_text: 放寬之後能過關的寫法，作者列了四種
claims.evidence: Take a parameter pointing at an object, and another parameter pointing somewhere inside that object, and write through only the latter (we'll see this in the next section).
claims.note: Source bullet list has FIVE patterns; the post omits this second one and states four. Say 'five' or 'among them four'. Ledger has no note for it.

claims.claim_text: 零執行期成本的主張，作者自己承認「Though it's debatable if any language can get memory safety with zero run-time cost.」
claims.evidence: Though it's debatable if any language can get memory safety with zero run-time cost.
claims.note: Hedge preserved; claim sits on the 'What group borrowing can do' lead, fn 16.

claims.claim_text: 作者說 group borrowing 把 shared-xor-mutable 放寬成 no use-after-free；編譯期抓 use-after-free 且限制比先前做法少
claims.location: under H2「和 Rust 的差別」para 1
claims.evidence: It catches use-after-free problems at compile time, and it does it in a way that has less restrictions than previous approaches.
claims.note: The post's gloss of shared-xor-mutable and 'the four patterns violate the former but not the latter' is the post's reading (fn 19/21 support rollback/structs only); low risk.

claims.claim_text: 同一 step 例子比較 C++、Rust、GhostCell、Valen，定性、無 benchmark；Rust「memory-safe, but a little slower, and a little more complex」；GhostCell「the same speed as C++, but it's still a bit complex」；Valen「fast, safe, and simple」；C++ 要靠人維持安全
claims.location: under H2「和 Rust 的差別」para 2 + table
claims.evidence: Adding GhostCell gave us the same speed as C++, but it's still a bit complex.
claims.note: Table 'C++ faster/simpler than Rust' backed by n64; 'no benchmark numbers' holds.

claims.claim_text: Rust 版慢的原因他在註腳說得具體（需丟掉 &mut 再重取、每次取用帶 bounds check）；扁平化的取捨：節點不隨父節點自動刪除、拆太細可能 ID chasing cache miss
claims.location: under H2「和 Rust 的差別」para 2
claims.evidence: nodes aren't automatically deleted when their parents are. Also, if you split into parallel collections too much, you might risk "ID chasing" cache-miss slowdowns.
claims.note: Trace failure: fn 26/27 content has no ledger notes. Also 'bounds check' comes from the Rust code comments, not footnote 26. Content otherwise matches; add notes and fix attribution.

claims.claim_text: 讀這張表要留意作者自己加的兩道保險：「This won't necessarily mean Valen will be faster than C++, Rust, etc.」「I think you can do extra refactoring or use unsafe…」，後一句承認別的語言靠多花功夫也能追平
claims.location: under H2「和 Rust 的差別」para 3
claims.evidence: This won't necessarily mean Valen will be faster than C++, Rust, etc. I think you can do extra refactoring or use unsafe in those languages to get equivalent speedups.
claims.note: Context drift: fn 43 qualifies the OPTIMIZER benefit of mutable-in-immutable, not the step comparison table. The table-relevant caveat is fn 29 ('You can generally rearrange your Rust code to match group borrowing's speed'). Re-scope or re-source.

claims.claim_text: Valen 做法建立在朋友 Nick Smith 設計的 Group Borrowing 提案上，「originally designed with Mojo in mind」，作者盡力仍沒說服 higher-ups，「Group borrowing was dead before it had the chance to succeed.」
claims.location: under H2「和 Rust 的差別」para 4
claims.evidence: It was originally designed with Mojo in mind , but alas, despite my best efforts I couldn't convince the higher-ups that we should use it.

claims.claim_text: 作者列：Google 的 Carbon「pivoted completely to group borrowing」、Plecra 的 exclusion typing「redesigning the Rust borrow checker with concepts from group borrowing and GhostCell」；post 註明是作者轉述、未查證
claims.location: under H2「和 Rust 的差別」para 4
claims.evidence: Google's Carbon language pivoted completely to group borrowing (and even credited our article, which was nice of them!)

claims.claim_text: 局部的 mut 讓 step 只動到一個元素，其餘的參照都不受牽連
claims.evidence: This is good because this won't invalidate callers' references to entities.
claims.note: Overgeneralization: the post's own figure shows step still invalidates R3 (refs inside the element). Source only says references to the entities (not inside them) survive. Restate to what the source says. The purpose quote itself (n35) is exact.

claims.claim_text: 作者說更細的資訊可能對最佳化器有用：「I suspect this feature could make Valen code optimize better.」；可能需要修補 LLVM（noalias 而非 read-only）
claims.evidence: This might require patches to LLVM to make it better able to harness the information. It tends to think in terms of noalias , not in terms of "read-only".
claims.note: Hedging preserved.

claims.claim_text: 另外「we should be careful here too, because that same purpose can be served by other features in theory」(作為最佳化器好處的第二個但書)
claims.evidence: I suspect this will be useful for more than just Rust interop. It could erase inner details from signatures... However, we should be careful here too, because that same purpose can be served by other features in theory.
claims.note: Citation drift: this sentence is in the Wildcard Descendant Paths section about signature erasure, not about optimizer benefits. Delete or re-attribute.

claims.claim_text: Rust 互通規則：唯一能到達資料的 Valen 參照可交給 Rust &mut；多個可能指向同一物件時只能交給 &
claims.evidence: If we have multiple Valen references that can point to the same object, they can only be handed into Rust & references.

claims.claim_text: 作者推測 Valen 可有類似「unique group」的東西，讓程式碼明講某個群組在呼叫期間是唯一的（構想，未做）

claims.evidence: Valen now interprets the above Rust function as if it were this:
